explain.fr: À partir de « patient », on forme « patience ».

question: His ___ was a surprise to everyone. (DECIDE)

explain.fr: À partir de « decide », on forme « decision ».

question: The government promised ___ for all. (EQUAL)

explain.fr: À partir de « equal », on forme « equality ».

explain.fr: À partir de « polite », on forme « impolite ».

question: The answer was ___. (CORRECT)

explain.fr: À partir de « correct », on forme « incorrect ».

question: I ___ with your opinion. (AGREE)

explain.fr: À partir de « agree », on forme « disagree ».

question: He is ___ for the project. (RESPONSIBLE)
fr: Il est responsable du projet.

explain.fr: À partir de « responsible », on forme « responsible ».

question: The story is completely ___. (BELIEVE)

explain.fr: À partir de « believe », on forme « unbelievable ».

question: She works as a ___. (JOURNAL)
fr: Elle travaille comme journaliste.

explain.fr: À partir de « journal », on forme « journalist ».

question: The ___ of the city has grown. (POPULATE)
fr: La population de la ville a augmenté.

explain.fr: À partir de « populate », on forme « population ».

say: The population of the city has grown.

question: We had a long ___. (DISCUSS)
fr: Nous avons eu une longue discussion.

explain.fr: À partir de « discuss », on forme « discussion ».

question: Smoking is ___ to your health. (HARM)
fr: Fumer est nocif pour la santé.

explain.fr: À partir de « harm », on forme « harmful ».

say: Smoking is harmful to your health.

question: The ___ of the experiment was clear. (SIGNIFY)
fr: L'importance de l'expérience était claire.

explain.fr: À partir de « signify », on forme « significance ».

say: The significance of the experiment was clear.

question: If I had known about the party, I ___.
fr: Si j'avais su pour la fête, je serais venu.

explain.fr: Conditionnel 3 (passé irréel) : if + past perfect, would have + participe.
explain.en: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + participle.

say: If I had known about the party, I would have come.

question: If she ___ harder, she would have passed.
fr: Si elle avait travaillé davantage, elle aurait réussi.

explain.fr: Après « if » au conditionnel 3 : past perfect.
explain.en: After “if” in the third conditional: past perfect.

say: If she had studied harder, she would have passed.

question: If I had taken that job, I ___ in New York now.
fr: Si j'avais accepté ce poste, je vivrais à New York maintenant.

explain.fr: Conditionnel mixte : passé irréel → conséquence présente (would + verbe).
explain.en: Mixed conditional: unreal past → present result (would + verb).

say: If I had taken that job, I would be living in New York now.

question: ___ you need any help, please let me know.
fr: Si vous avez besoin d'aide, n'hésitez pas à me le dire.

explain.fr: Should + sujet = if (style soutenu).

say: Should you need any help, please let me know.

question: I'll lend you the money ___ you pay me back next week.
fr: Je te prêterai l'argent à condition que tu me rembourses la semaine prochaine.

explain.fr: provided (that) = à condition que.

say: I'll lend you the money provided you pay me back next week.

question: Take a map ___ you get lost.
fr: Prends une carte au cas où tu te perdrais.

explain.fr: in case = au cas où (précaution).

say: Take a map in case you get lost.

question: I wish I ___ to the party last night.
fr: Je regrette de ne pas être allé à la fête hier soir.

explain.fr: Regret sur le passé : wish + past perfect.
explain.en: Regret about the past: wish + past perfect.

say: I wish I had gone to the party last night.

question: I wish you ___ making that noise!
fr: J'aimerais que tu arrêtes de faire ce bruit !

explain.fr: Agacement / souhait de changement de l'autre : wish + would.
explain.en: Annoyance / wanting someone else to change: wish + would.

say: I wish you would stop making that noise!

question: If only I ___ more time!
fr: Si seulement j'avais plus de temps !

explain.fr: If only + prétérit (présent irréel).

say: If only I had more time!

question: It's time we ___ home.
fr: Il est temps que nous rentrions.

explain.fr: It's (high) time + sujet + prétérit.

question: I'd rather you ___ tell anyone.
fr: Je préférerais que tu ne le dises à personne.

explain.fr: I'd rather + autre sujet + prétérit.

say: I'd rather you didn't tell anyone.

question: The report ___ by Friday.
fr: Le rapport doit être terminé d'ici vendredi.

explain.fr: Modal + passif : modal + be + participe.

say: The report must be finished by Friday.

question: The house ___ since last year.
fr: La maison est vide depuis l'année dernière.

explain.fr: « depuis » : present perfect (has been).

say: The house has been empty since last year.

question: A new hospital ___ at the moment.
fr: Un nouvel hôpital est en construction.

explain.fr: Passif progressif : is being + participe.

say: A new hospital is being built at the moment.

question: He ___ to have stolen the money.
fr: On pense qu'il a volé l'argent.

explain.fr: « On pense que » : sujet + is believed + to have + participe.
explain.en: “It is believed that…”: subject + is believed + to have + participle.

say: He is believed to have stolen the money.

question: The documents ___ before the meeting.
fr: Les documents avaient été envoyés avant la réunion.

explain.fr: Passif au past perfect : had been + participe.
explain.en: Past perfect passive: had been + participle.

say: The documents had been sent before the meeting.

question: I hate ___ what to do.
fr: Je déteste qu'on me dise quoi faire.

explain.fr: Gérondif passif : being + participe.

say: I hate being told what to do.

question: She ___ her bag stolen on the subway.
fr: Elle s'est fait voler son sac dans le métro.

explain.fr: have something done : subir quelque chose (aussi « get »).
explain.en: have something done: something happens to you (also “get”).

say: She had her bag stolen on the subway.

question: I need to get my car ___.
fr: Je dois faire réparer ma voiture.

explain.fr: get + objet + participe passé.

say: I need to get my car repaired.

question: I'll get my brother ___ me move.
fr: Je vais demander à mon frère de m'aider à déménager.

explain.fr: get + personne + to + verbe (persuader quelqu'un).

say: I'll get my brother to help me move.

question: She ___ have forgotten; she never forgets anything.
fr: Elle ne peut pas avoir oublié ; elle n'oublie jamais rien.

explain.fr: Déduction négative sur le passé : can't have + participe.
explain.en: Negative deduction about the past: can't have + participle.

say: She can't have forgotten; she never forgets anything.

question: The streets are wet. It ___ have rained.
fr: Les rues sont mouillées. Il a dû pleuvoir.

explain.fr: Déduction positive sur le passé : must have + participe.
explain.en: Positive deduction about the past: must have + participle.

say: The streets are wet. It must have rained.

question: He ___ have taken the train, but I'm not sure.
fr: Il a peut-être pris le train, mais je n'en suis pas sûr.

explain.fr: Possibilité passée : might / may have + participe.
explain.en: Past possibility: might / may have + participle.

say: He might have taken the train, but I'm not sure.

question: You ___ have bought milk. We already had some.
fr: Tu n'avais pas besoin d'acheter du lait. On en avait déjà.

explain.fr: Action inutile mais faite : needn't have + participe.
explain.en: Unnecessary action that was done: needn't have + participle.

say: You needn't have bought milk. We already had some.

question: We ___ to wear a tie at work, but most people do.
fr: Nous ne sommes pas censés porter de cravate au travail, mais la plupart le font.

explain.fr: be supposed to = être censé.
explain.en: be supposed to = be expected to.

say: We aren't supposed to wear a tie at work, but most people do.

question: Despite the storm, they ___ reach the village.
fr: Malgré la tempête, ils ont réussi à atteindre le village.

explain.fr: Réussite ponctuelle dans le passé : was / were able to (et non could).
explain.en: One-off past success: was / were able to (not could).

say: Despite the storm, they were able to reach the village.

question: I object to ___ like a child.
fr: Je refuse d'être traité comme un enfant.

explain.fr: object to + -ing (passif : being + participe).

say: I object to being treated like a child.

question: She admitted ___ the window.
fr: Elle a avoué avoir cassé la vitre.

explain.fr: admit + -ing.

question: He denied ___ the money.
fr: Il a nié avoir pris l'argent.

explain.fr: deny + -ing (having + participe pour l'antériorité).
explain.en: deny + -ing (having + participle for an earlier action).

say: He denied having taken the money.

question: I regret ___ you that your application was unsuccessful.
fr: J'ai le regret de vous informer que votre candidature n'a pas été retenue.

explain.fr: regret + to = avoir le regret de (annonce).

say: I regret to inform you that your application was unsuccessful.

question: I regret ___ so rude to her.
fr: Je regrette d'avoir été si impoli avec elle.

explain.fr: regret + -ing = regretter une action passée.
explain.en: regret + -ing = be sorry about a past action.

say: I regret being so rude to her.

question: Try ___ the computer off and on again.
fr: Essaie d'éteindre et de rallumer l'ordinateur.

explain.fr: try + -ing = essayer (pour voir si ça marche).

say: Try turning the computer off and on again.

question: I tried ___ the box, but it was too heavy.
fr: J'ai essayé de soulever la boîte, mais elle était trop lourde.

explain.fr: try + to = s'efforcer de (difficulté).

say: I tried to lift the box, but it was too heavy.

question: She's used to ___ early.
fr: Elle a l'habitude de se lever tôt.

explain.fr: be used to + -ing = avoir l'habitude de.
explain.en: be used to + -ing = be accustomed to.

say: She's used to getting up early.

question: I'll never get used to ___ on the left.
fr: Je ne m'habituerai jamais à conduire à gauche.

explain.fr: get used to + -ing = s'habituer à.
explain.en: get used to + -ing = become accustomed to.

say: I'll never get used to driving on the left.

question: He seems ___ a lot of weight.
fr: Il semble avoir perdu beaucoup de poids.

explain.fr: seem + to have + participe (antériorité).

say: He seems to have lost a lot of weight.

question: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot the tickets.
fr: Non seulement il est arrivé en retard, mais il a aussi oublié les billets.

explain.fr: Not only en tête : inversion (auxiliaire + sujet).
explain.en: Not only at the start: inversion (auxiliary + subject).

say: Not only did he arrive late, but he also forgot the tickets.

question: Hardly ___ when the phone rang.
fr: À peine m'étais-je assis que le téléphone a sonné.

explain.fr: Hardly / Scarcely… when : inversion au past perfect.
explain.en: Hardly / Scarcely… when: inversion with past perfect.

say: Hardly had I sat down when the phone rang.

question: Never ___ such a beautiful sunset.
fr: Je n'ai jamais vu un aussi beau coucher de soleil.

explain.fr: Adverbe négatif en tête : inversion.
explain.en: Negative adverb at the start: inversion.

say: Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.

question: Little ___ that they were being watched.
fr: Ils étaient loin de se douter qu'on les observait.

explain.fr: Little en tête (sens négatif) : inversion avec did.
explain.en: “Little” at the start (negative meaning): inversion with did.

say: Little did they know that they were being watched.

question: It was my sister ___ told me.
fr: C'est ma sœur qui me l'a dit.

explain.fr: Mise en relief (cleft) : It was + personne + who.
explain.en: Cleft sentence: It was + person + who.

say: It was my sister who told me.

question: ___ I need is a vacation.
fr: Ce dont j'ai besoin, ce sont des vacances.

explain.fr: Mise en relief : What + sujet + verbe + is…

say: What I need is a vacation.

question: My brother, ___ lives in Canada, is visiting us.
fr: Mon frère, qui vit au Canada, nous rend visite.

explain.fr: Relative explicative (entre virgules) : who / which, jamais « that ».
explain.en: Non-defining clause (with commas): who / which, never “that”.

say: My brother, who lives in Canada, is visiting us.

question: She passed the exam, ___ surprised everyone.
fr: Elle a réussi l'examen, ce qui a surpris tout le monde.

explain.fr: « ce qui » reprenant toute une proposition : , which.
explain.en: “Ce qui” referring to a whole clause: , which.

say: She passed the exam, which surprised everyone.

question: The person to ___ I spoke was very helpful.
fr: La personne à qui j'ai parlé a été très serviable.

explain.fr: Après une préposition : whom (personne) / which (chose).

say: The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.

question: The reason ___ I called is to invite you.
fr: La raison pour laquelle j'ai appelé, c'est pour t'inviter.

explain.fr: the reason why = la raison pour laquelle.

say: The reason why I called is to invite you.

question: I have two brothers, both of ___ are doctors.
fr: J'ai deux frères, tous deux médecins.

explain.fr: Quantifieur + of whom / of which.

say: I have two brothers, both of whom are doctors.

question: He asked me ___ I had seen the film.
fr: Il m'a demandé si j'avais vu le film.

explain.fr: Question fermée rapportée : if / whether.

say: He asked me whether I had seen the film.

question: She said she ___ the day before.
fr: Elle a dit qu'elle était arrivée la veille.

explain.fr: Prétérit → past perfect au discours indirect.
explain.en: Past simple → past perfect in reported speech.

say: She said she had arrived the day before.

question: He suggested that we ___ a taxi.
fr: Il a suggéré que nous prenions un taxi.

explain.fr: suggest that + sujet + verbe de base (ou should + verbe).
explain.en: suggest that + subject + base verb (or should + verb).

say: He suggested that we take a taxi.

question: They accused him ___ lying.
fr: Ils l'ont accusé de mentir.

explain.fr: accuse someone of + -ing.

question: She apologized ___ late.
fr: Elle s'est excusée d'être en retard.

explain.fr: apologize for + -ing.

question: ___ hard I try, I can't remember his name.
fr: J'ai beau essayer, je n'arrive pas à me souvenir de son nom.

explain.fr: However + adjectif / adverbe = si… que, avoir beau.
explain.en: However + adjective / adverb = no matter how.

say: However hard I try, I can't remember his name.

question: ___ happens, I'll be there for you.
fr: Quoi qu'il arrive, je serai là pour toi.

explain.fr: Whatever = quoi que.

say: Whatever happens, I'll be there for you.

question: She was successful ___ her lack of experience.
fr: Elle a réussi malgré son manque d'expérience.

explain.fr: in spite of / despite + nom.

say: She was successful in spite of her lack of experience.

question: He's very rich, ___ his brother is quite poor.
fr: Il est très riche, alors que son frère est plutôt pauvre.

explain.fr: Contraste entre deux faits : whereas / while.
explain.en: Contrast between two facts: whereas / while.

say: He's very rich, whereas his brother is quite poor.

question: We should leave now; ___, we'll miss the train.
fr: Nous devrions partir maintenant, sinon nous allons rater le train.

explain.fr: « sinon » = otherwise.

say: We should leave now; otherwise, we'll miss the train.

question: The flight was canceled ___ the fog.
fr: Le vol a été annulé à cause du brouillard.

explain.fr: due to / because of + nom.

say: The flight was canceled due to the fog.

question: He studied hard ___ pass the exam.

question:
Over the past twenty years, clothes have become cheaper and fashion trends have changed faster than ever. Some brands now release new collections every week. This model, known as fast fashion, has made it possible for almost anyone to follow trends, but it comes at a high cost. The textile industry is one of the most polluting in the world, using huge quantities of water and producing tons of waste. Most cheap garments are worn only a few times before being thrown away. In response, a growing number of consumers are turning to second-hand clothes, renting outfits for special occasions or simply buying fewer, better-quality items.

What is fast fashion?
fr: Lisez le texte, puis répondez : Qu'est-ce que la « fast fashion » ?
answer: A model where trends and collections change very quickly

question:
Electric cars, once a rarity, are now a common sight in many cities. Governments are encouraging drivers to switch by offering subsidies and building charging stations, and several countries plan to ban the sale of new gasoline and diesel cars within the next decade. Supporters argue that electric vehicles reduce air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. Critics, however, point out that producing batteries requires rare metals whose extraction can damage the environment. They also note that electric cars are only as clean as the electricity used to charge them. Despite these concerns, sales continue to rise year after year.

How are governments encouraging people to buy electric cars?
fr: Lisez le texte, puis répondez : Comment les gouvernements encouragent-ils l'achat de voitures électriques ?

explain.fr: Réponse : « Through subsidies and charging stations ». Relisez le passage du texte qui en parle.

question:
According to researchers, about forty percent of our daily actions are not real decisions but habits. A habit is formed through a simple loop: a cue triggers a routine, which leads to a reward. For example, feeling tired in the afternoon (the cue) may lead you to buy a coffee (the routine), which gives you energy (the reward). To change a bad habit, experts suggest keeping the same cue and reward but replacing the routine, such as going for a short walk instead of drinking coffee. Building a new habit takes time: one study found it takes on average sixty-six days.

What proportion of daily actions are habits?

Others were evacuated after natural disasters or industrial accidents. Today, a few of these places attract curious tourists who enjoy exploring empty streets and crumbling buildings. question:
Before booking a hotel or trying a new restaurant, most of us read online reviews. Studies show that consumers trust them almost as much as personal recommendations from friends. However, not all reviews are genuine. Some businesses pay people to write positive comments about them or negative ones about their competitors. Websites use algorithms to detect suspicious reviews, but fake ones still slip through. Experts advise reading a wide range of reviews, paying attention to detailed comments and being wary of extremely enthusiastic ones written in a similar style.

How much do consumers trust online reviews?

answer: Almost as much as friends' recommendations

In cities around the world, empty lots and rooftops are being turned into vegetable gardens. These urban gardens provide fresh, local food in neighborhoods where supermarkets are rare or expensive. They also bring residents together: neighbors who had never spoken to each other now share tools, seeds and advice. Studies suggest that gardening reduces stress and encourages healthier eating. Although urban gardens cannot feed entire cities, their supporters believe they play an important role in making cities greener and more pleasant places to live.

question:
Platforms that allow people to rent out their homes, cars or even tools to strangers have grown enormously in the last decade. For owners, they are a way to earn extra income from things they rarely use; for users, they offer cheaper and more flexible options than traditional businesses. Yet the sharing economy has its downsides. In popular tourist cities, short-term rentals have reduced the number of homes available to local residents and pushed up rents. Several cities have therefore introduced rules limiting the number of nights a property can be rented each year.

question:
A job interview can be stressful, but good preparation makes a big difference. First, research the company: candidates who know about its products and values make a much better impression. Second, prepare examples of situations where you have shown key skills, such as teamwork or problem-solving. Third, think about questions to ask at the end; it shows that you are genuinely interested. Finally, don't underestimate body language. A firm handshake, eye contact and a smile can be just as important as what you say.
